title: HINT for Product Managers — PRDs keep their intent
metaDescription: Keep goals, personas, stories, non-goals and sourced metrics beside PRDs so assistants expose trade-offs instead of making them silently.
h1: Your assistant drafts PRDs fast. HINT keeps the product intent intact.
intro: HINT stores goals, personas, non-goals, metrics and decisions as plain-text notes beside product documents. Your assistant reads the relevant product context before refining a story or roadmap.

situations.before: A polished story targets a persona nobody defined.
situations.after: Every story points to a real persona
situations.body: The assistant uses only the declared audience and turns missing user context into a decision needed from the team.

situations.before: A success metric arrives with an invented baseline.
situations.body: A number without a source stays an open question instead of becoming a credible-looking KPI.

situations.before: A nice-to-have quietly enters the committed scope.
situations.body: Trade-offs are surfaced for the product owner rather than settled invisibly during drafting.

example.intro: The Hooli demo pins a Nucleus story to an approved product source.
example.after: It drafts criteria that stay inside the product scope and refuses to add a persona, baseline or trade-off decision that SRC-1 does not support.
example.compiled:
<story name="nucleus-1">
  Approved story grounded in SRC-1.
</story>
<never name="Invented details">…</never>

never: Invent a persona, metric baseline or research finding.
Promote optional work without an explicit priority decision.
Pull a declared non-goal back into scope.
disclaimer: HINT keeps product intent visible to an assistant; discovery, prioritization and outcome ownership remain with the product team.

faq.a: It can help your assistant draft one from declared product context and create a derivable skeleton where an emit pack applies.
No. It presents declared priorities and marks unresolved trade-offs as decisions needed.

faq.q: Can PM and engineering books work together?
faq.a: Yes. Product stories and engineering contracts can share the common core while retaining their specialist vocabulary.

keywordDescriptions.product: Sets the product area whose context applies.
keywordDescriptions.persona: Defines a user group from known research.
keywordDescriptions.goal: States the measurable outcome the work serves.
keywordDescriptions.metric: Defines a measure together with its baseline source.
keywordDescriptions.story: Records a user story with a stable identifier.
keywordDescriptions.criteria: Sets testable acceptance conditions for a story.
keywordDescriptions.hypothesis: States a belief that an experiment can test.
keywordDescriptions.launch: Collects explicit go and no-go conditions.
